UPSTREAM: soc/intel/common: Move update_mrc_cache after BS_DEV_ENUMERATE This patch ensures that MRC cache data is already written into SPI chip before SPI protected regions are getting locked during BS_DEV_RESOURCES-BS_ON_EXIT. This requirements are intended to support platform security guideline where all required chipset registers are expected to be in lock down stage before launching any 3rd party code as in option rom etc. coreboot has to change its execution order to meet those requirements. Hence storing mrc cache data into SPI has been moved right after pci enumeration is done, so that SPI registers can be lock down before calling post pci enumeration FSP NotifyPhase() API which is targeted to be done in BS_DEV_ENABLE-BS_ON_ENTRY. TEST=Ensure MRC training data is stored into SPI chip and power_ Resume autotest is passing. Change-Id: I9ecc2ba2adf3f2167ebad71d29a271b2589e4e04 Signed-off-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@google.com> Original-Commit-Id: 2d1dd5943d12a6ef46ab6d3d580545e89622e47d Original-Change-Id: I8ee26b5cc70433438cf4e45e707b8a54f89cf9b0 Original-Signed-off-by: Subrata Banik <subrata.banik@intel.com> Original-Reviewed-on: https://review.coreboot.org/21028 Original-Tested-by: build bot (Jenkins) <no-reply@coreboot.org> Original-Reviewed-by: Aaron Durbin <adurbin@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/636968 Commit-Ready: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Tested-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Patrick Georgi <pgeorgi@chromium.org>

UPSTREAM: soc/intel/skylake: Move DMI lock down config after resource allocation This patch to ensures that coreboot is performing DMI registers lockdown after PCI enumeration is done. This requirements are intended to support platform security guideline where all required chipset registers are expected to be in lock down stage before launching any 3rd party code as in option rom etc. coreboot has to change its execution order to meet those requirements. Hence BIOS Interface lock down through Sideband access has been moved right after pci resource allocation is done, so that BILD lock down is getting executed along with LPC and SPI BIOS interface lockdown settings before calling post pci enumeration FSP NotifyPhase() API which is targeted to be done in BS_DEV_ENABLE-BS_ON_ENTRY. TEST=Ensure DMI register offset 0x274c bit 0 is set. hammerd: Refactor the structure of hammer_updater_unittest. Originally, the calling structure of HammerUpdater is: Run() => RunLoop() => RunOnce() Since RunLoop only iterately call the Run() method, so we don't test it directly. Therefore, we had two-layer unittest: - Test Run() method: (HammerUpdaterFlowTest) mock RunOnce() and data members. - Test RunOnce() method: (HammerUpdaterFullTest) only mock data members. We will start to implement PostRWProcess() later. The logic is quite irrelevant to the firmware updating, so we split the unittest for them. Now the calling structure becomes: Run() => RunLoop() => RunOnce() => PostRWProcess() The structure of unittest becomes: - Test Run() method: (HammerUpdaterFlowTest) - Mainly test the interaction between Run() and RunOnce() - Mock RunOnce() and data members. - Test RunOnce() method: (HammerUpdaterRWTest) - Mainly test the interaction between RunOnce and external interface - One exception: Test a special sequence that needs to reset 3 times called by Run(). - Mock PostRWProcess() and data members. - Test PostRWProcess() method: (HammerUpdaterPostRWTest) - Test the interaction between PostRWProcess and external interface - only mock all external data members. Also removed the unused FRIEND_TEST declaration.
